assumptions: A-POL-01: Observation layout is stable at 301 bytes (CHESS_OBS_SIZE). Any change to C obs layout must bump a version constant and all policies must be updated.
A-POL-02: Action space is stable at 97 discrete actions (64 squares + 32 promotions + 1 pass). All policies produce logits of shape [B, 97].
A-POL-03: PufferLib CLI resolves policy via `getattr(env_module.torch, args['policy_name'])`. Ocean envs use `pufferlib/ocean/torch.py`. External envs use `pufferlib/environments/{package}/torch.py`.
A-POL-04: PufferLib's encode_observations/decode_actions pattern is required for LSTMWrapper compatibility. All policies must implement this interface.
A-POL-05: The action masking logic is part of the policy (computed in encode_observations, applied in decode_actions). All policies must implement the same masking contract.
A-POL-06: config/chess.ini `policy_name` field selects the policy class by name. `rnn_name` selects the LSTM wrapper. These are resolved via getattr on the torch module.
A-POL-07: install_cli.py appends policy code to ocean/torch.py. Multiple policies can coexist as separate classes in this file.

A-POL-08: Checkpoint compatibility requires matching state_dict keys. Changing policy architecture means new checkpoints; old checkpoints cannot load into architecturally different policies without explicit migration.
A-POL-09: Two integration paths exist: (1) standalone train_chess.py (imports Policy directly), (2) PufferLib CLI (imports from ocean/torch.py via config). Both must be supported.

changes.title: Define stable policy interface (ObsContract + ActionContract)
changes.description: Create a formal interface/base class that all chess policies must implement. This defines the obs->policy and policy->action contracts.

required_methods.encode_observations(x, state=None) -> hi: Parse 301-byte obs, build action mask, store as self._action_mask, return hidden tensor of shape [B, hidden_size]
required_methods.decode_actions(hidden) -> (logits, value: Produce logits [B, 97] with action mask applied, value [B, 1]

obs_parsing_contract.board: x[:, 0:64] - uint8 piece codes (0-12), parsed to board representation

interface_spec.action_mask_contract: In encode_observations: build self._action_mask [B, 97] bool tensor. Phase 0: mask[:, :64] = valid_pieces. Phase 1: mask[:, :64] = valid_dests, mask[:, 64:96] = valid_promos. mask[:, 96] = pass_valid. In decode_actions: apply mask via masked_fill(~mask, -1e9) with all-masked fallback.

acceptance: All policies implement encode_observations/decode_actions
All policies correctly parse the 301-byte observation
All policies produce [B, 97] logits with proper masking
All policies are LSTMWrapper-compatible

changes.title: Extract shared obs parsing and action masking into a reusable mixin or helper
changes.description: The obs parsing (301 bytes -> board, scalars, masks) and action mask building logic is identical across all policies. Extract it into a ChessObsParser helper class or mixin to avoid duplication.

details.approach: Create a ChessObsMixin or standalone parse_chess_obs() function that all policies can use. This parses raw uint8 obs into named tensors (board, side, castling, etc.) and builds the action mask.
details.location: train_chess.py (top-level helper) and mirrored in install_cli.py CHESS_POLICY_CONTENT

components.parse_obs(x): Returns dict of named tensors: board_oh [B,13,8,8], side [B,2], castling [B,4], etc.

acceptance: Helper function exists and is tested
All policies use the shared parser instead of duplicating obs-slice logic
Action mask construction is consistent across all policies

changes.title: ChessConvResNet policy (current default, renamed for clarity)
changes.description: The current Policy class uses CNN + residual blocks for board encoding + scalar MLP. Rename to ChessConvResNet for the registry and keep as default.

architecture_summary.spatial_input: 13 one-hot piece channels + valid_pieces plane + valid_dests plane + selected plane = 16 channels
architecture_summary.scalar_input: side(2) + castling(4) + ep(1) + phase(2) + check(2) + rule50(1) + pass_valid(1) + promos(32) = 45

acceptance: Existing checkpoints continue to load with both 'Chess' and 'ChessConvResNet' names
Default config still uses this architecture
No performance regression

changes.title: ChessNNUE policy architecture
changes.description: NNUE-style policy inspired by Stockfish NNUE. Uses piece-on-square feature encoding with efficient sparse input.

architecture_concept.feature_encoding: HalfKP-lite: for each (king_square, piece_type, piece_square) triple, compute a feature index. Use nn.EmbeddingBag for sparse-to-dense. ~768 input features (own king sq 64 * 12 piece types = 768 possible features, typically ~16 active).
architecture_concept.layers: Linear(768, 512) -> ClippedReLU -> Linear(512, 256) -> ClippedReLU -> Linear(256, hidden_size)
architecture_concept.advantages: Very fast inference (no convolutions), sparse input, proven effective for chess evaluation
architecture_concept.disadvantages: Less spatial awareness than CNN, may need more training data

details.risk: medium - new architecture, needs training validation

acceptance: Policy passes forward/backward with correct shapes
Trains to at least 50% win rate vs random in 1M steps
Inference faster than ChessConvResNet (no convolutions)

changes.title: ChessResNet policy architecture (deeper residual tower)
changes.description: AlphaZero-lite residual tower with more blocks and larger channel count. For research/scaling experiments.

architecture_concept.tower: Conv2d(16, 128, 3x3) -> N ResidualBlocks(128) where N=4,8,16 configurable
architecture_concept.residual_block: Conv2d(128, 128, 3x3, pad=1) -> BatchNorm -> ReLU -> Conv2d(128, 128, 3x3, pad=1) -> BatchNorm -> skip-add -> ReLU
architecture_concept.value_head: Conv2d(128, 1, 1x1) -> BatchNorm -> ReLU -> flatten -> Linear(64, 256) -> ReLU -> Linear(256, 1) -> tanh
architecture_concept.advantages: Proven AlphaZero architecture, scalable with depth/width
architecture_concept.disadvantages: Larger model, slower per-step, needs more compute

details.risk: medium - well-understood architecture but needs tuning

acceptance: Configurable depth/width via policy config
Trains successfully with PPO self-play
Scales GPU utilization appropriately

changes.title: ChessTransformer policy architecture
changes.description: Attention-based policy treating board squares as tokens. Experimental.

architecture_concept.tokenization: 64 board squares -> 64 tokens. Each token = nn.Embedding(13, d_model) + positional encoding (learned or sinusoidal for 8x8 grid)
architecture_concept.encoder: N transformer encoder layers (d_model=128, nhead=4, dim_ff=512). N=2-4.
architecture_concept.global_token: Prepend a [CLS] token that aggregates board state. Scalar features injected here.
architecture_concept.policy_head: Use per-square token outputs for square selection (phase 0/1), [CLS] for value
architecture_concept.action_decoding: Phase 0: dot(square_tokens, query_vector) -> 64 logits. Phase 1: same for dests + promo head.
architecture_concept.advantages: Can learn long-range piece interactions, attention maps interpretable
architecture_concept.disadvantages: More compute per step than CNN, harder to tune, may overfit on small batch

details.risk: high - experimental, may not converge with PPO self-play

acceptance: Forward/backward passes work
Attention maps can be extracted for interpretability
Trains to at least random-beating performance

changes.title: Policy registry system with config-based selection
changes.description: Implement a registry that maps policy_name strings to policy classes. Support both CLI (ocean/torch.py) and standalone (train_chess.py) paths.

mechanism.registry_dict: CHESS_POLICIES = {'Chess': ChessConvResNet, 'ChessConvResNet': ChessConvResNet, 'ChessNNUE': ChessNNUE, 'ChessResNet': ChessResNet, 'ChessTransformer': ChessTransformer}
mechanism.cli_path: PufferLib resolves via `getattr(ocean.torch, policy_name)`. Each policy class is a top-level name in ocean/torch.py. No special registry needed for CLI - just define the classes.
mechanism.standalone_path: In train_chess.py, add a get_policy(name, env, **kwargs) factory function that looks up CHESS_POLICIES[name]
mechanism.config_integration: chess.ini [base] policy_name = Chess (default). Override with CLI: puffer train puffer_chess --policy-name ChessNNUE
mechanism.rnn_wrapper: Each policy needs a matching LSTM wrapper (or reuse ChessLSTM since LSTMWrapper is generic). config [base] rnn_name = ChessLSTM works for all since LSTMWrapper only needs hidden_size.

details.risk: low - builds on existing PufferLib conventions

acceptance: All four policies loadable via config policy_name
CLI `puffer train puffer_chess --policy-name X` works for all X
Standalone `python train_chess.py --policy X` works for all X
Default (no override) still uses ChessConvResNet

changes.title: Checkpoint compatibility and versioning
changes.description: Establish conventions for checkpoint compatibility across policy versions.

conventions.obs_version: Integer version of the observation layout. Currently v1 (301 bytes). Bumped whenever obs layout changes.
conventions.policy_name_in_checkpoint: Store the policy class name so loaders know which architecture to instantiate
conventions.strict_loading: Use strict=True by default. If obs_version mismatches, error with clear message.
conventions.migration_path: When obs layout changes: (1) bump obs_version, (2) provide a migrate_checkpoint(old_ckpt, new_obs_version) utility if feasible, (3) document in CHANGELOG

details.cross_policy_notes: Checkpoints are NOT compatible across different policy architectures (different state_dict keys). A ChessConvResNet checkpoint cannot load into ChessNNUE. This is by design - each architecture has its own training trajectory.
details.risk: low - convention only, no code changes needed now

acceptance: Checkpoint save includes policy_name and obs_version
Load code validates obs_version match
Clear error message if architecture mismatch

pufferlib_conventions_analysis.how_cli_resolves_policy: 1. Config .ini [base] has policy_name='Chess'. 2. pufferl.load_policy() does `getattr(env_module.torch, policy_name)` where env_module is pufferlib.ocean. 3. This looks up the class name in ocean/torch.py. 4. If rnn_name is set, wraps with `getattr(env_module.torch, rnn_name)`. 5. Policy kwargs come from [policy] section, rnn kwargs from [rnn] section.
pufferlib_conventions_analysis.ocean_torch_py_pattern: All ocean env policies live in a single file: pufferlib/ocean/torch.py. Each env's policies are separate classes (e.g., MOBA, Snake, Go, Chess). Policy classes follow encode_observations/decode_actions pattern.
pufferlib_conventions_analysis.external_env_pattern: External envs (atari, crafter, etc.) have their own torch.py in pufferlib/environments/{package}/torch.py.
pufferlib_conventions_analysis.our_integration: We use ocean path via install_cli.py which appends to ocean/torch.py. This means all policy classes must be defined in the CHESS_POLICY_CONTENT string literal in install_cli.py.
convention_notes: Policy __init__ takes (env, **kwargs) where env is the driver_env (has single_observation_space, single_action_space)
encode_observations and decode_actions are the split points for LSTM wrapping
hidden_size attribute must match LSTM input_size
is_continuous = False for discrete action spaces
PufferLib's sample_logits() handles discrete logits -> action sampling

current_architecture_analysis.lstm_wrapper: ChessLSTM (in train_chess.py, line 196) - thin wrapper around pufferlib.models.LSTMWrapper
current_architecture_analysis.instantiation: base_policy = Policy(vecenv, hidden_size=256, num_blocks=2); policy = ChessLSTM(vecenv, base_policy, 256, 256).to(device)
current_architecture_analysis.observation_flow: 301 uint8 bytes -> parse into board(64), side(2), castling(4), ep(1), phase(2), selected(64), valid_pieces(64), valid_dests(64), valid_promos(32), checks(2), rule50(1), pass(1) -> board one-hot 13ch + 3 spatial planes -> CNN -> flatten -> Linear(4096, 256) -> concat with scalar(45->64) -> fusion Linear(320, 256) -> hidden
current_architecture_analysis.action_flow: hidden -> Linear(256, 97) -> mask with stored _action_mask -> logits; Linear(256, 1) -> value
current_architecture_analysis.parameter_count: ~500K parameters (estimate: conv 16*64*9=9K, 2 res blocks 2*2*64*64*9=73K, proj 4096*256=1M, scalar 45*128+128*64=14K, fusion 320*256=82K, actor 256*97=25K, critic 256=256)
key_design_decisions: GroupNorm(8, 64) instead of BatchNorm - works with variable batch sizes
Action masking computed during encode_observations, stored as instance variable, applied during decode_actions
Batch size mismatch handling for LSTM training (B*T reshaping)

fighter_vs_ours_comparison.fighter_obs: 72 bytes: 64 board + 8 metadata (is_my_turn, 4 castling, ep, halfmove, fullmove)
fighter_vs_ours_comparison.our_obs: 301 bytes: 64 board + 237 metadata (includes phase, masks, selected piece, checks, promos, pass_valid)
fighter_vs_ours_comparison.fighter_actions: 4096 (from*64 + to), single-phase, illegal moves get random replacement
fighter_vs_ours_comparison.our_actions: 97, two-phase (pick piece then pick dest), action masking, no random replacement
fighter_vs_ours_comparison.fighter_policy: Embedding(13,32) -> MLP residual blocks (no CNN) -> Linear(hidden, 4096). Defined in ocean/torch.py class Chess.
fighter_vs_ours_comparison.our_policy: One-hot(13) -> CNN + residual -> Linear + scalar path -> fusion -> Linear(hidden, 97). Defined in train_chess.py class Policy.
fighter_vs_ours_comparison.key_difference: Fighter uses embedding + MLP (no spatial awareness). We use CNN + spatial planes (better for positional play). Fighter has 4096 action space, we have 97 with two-phase masking.
